clips.title: 沃什讲话定调：通胀目标重回PCE，市场会如何反应？

subtitles.en: Kevin, I want to start with you. It felt like listening to Warsh speak. Initially, I was like, oh, this is nothing, but nothing new. But the more I spoke with people afterwards, my mind changed. What was your takeaway initially?
subtitles.zh: 凯文，我想先请你谈谈。听沃什讲话，一开始我觉得没什么新意。但后来和人们交流后，我改变了看法。你最初的感受是什么？

subtitles.en: So I think that really this speech was the set of remarks we were looking for in July after that press conference. Essentially, I think right sizes and corrects for what was this ambiguous kind of message coming from the chair after that July decision to keep rates steady.
subtitles.zh: 我认为这次讲话正是我们在七月新闻发布会后期待的内容。基本上，它修正了七月维持利率不变后主席传递的模糊信号。

subtitles.en: I think more than cleared the bar for what the consensus was coming into this because there were a lot of questions over whether he was going to even talk about inflation and labor and the dynamics of the economy. So the fact that you did get this more laid out scenario and his economic analysis, I think is really him catching up to what the rest of the committee has been doing.
subtitles.zh: 我认为这远超市场共识预期，因为此前很多人质疑他是否会谈论通胀、劳动力以及经济动态。事实上，他给出了更详细的展望和经济分析，我认为这让他跟上了委员会其他成员的步伐。

subtitles.en: What are the drivers? Business investment being a strong one. Our financial conditions restrictive, him not seeing that right now, especially even with weakness and housing and agriculture he made that specific call out, even though you're seeing weakness there. I mean, that's where rate cuts would help. He's not seeing that as a case to be made that the broader economy is under this pressure from Fed policy right now.
subtitles.zh: 驱动因素是什么？商业活动是重要一环。他认为当前金融条件并非紧缩，尽管地产和农业领域出现疲软，他特别指出了这一点。但降息可能有助于这些领域，他并不认为整体经济正承受美联储政策的压力。

subtitles.en: So I do think that he certainly checked a lot of boxes in terms of what investors were looking for. And I think probably most importantly, really reaffirmed that commitment to PCE being the target and then 2% being also the inflation target. So the metric and also the rate of change. You know, firmly, I think we're committing to that was was crucial, because especially because in the last meeting. Again, there was a little bit of ambiguity around whether he was going to look at a different set of metrics and not necessarily PCE. Yeah, and I think when you look at those first remarks, and then these remarks, the thing that struck me is the pledge that he would take action, right? He says, you know, if if you don't have confidence, then we've got more work to do. I thought that was significant.
subtitles.zh: 我认为他确实满足了投资者的许多期待。最重要的是，他重申了以PCE为通胀目标、2%为目标的承诺。这一点至关重要，因为上次会议中，他是否会采用不同指标存在模糊性。而且，他承诺将采取行动，这很关键。

clips.title: 嘉信策略师：九月加息，数据说了算？

subtitles.en: And Kevin, I just want to come back to this whole idea of keeping an eye on that 2% inflation target, and what that ultimately means and expectations for, what is a very much live September meeting. Barclays came out saying they expect a hike in September and then another one in December. How are you thinking about the path forward?
subtitles.zh: 凯文，我想回到2%通胀目标的话题，以及这对九月会议意味着什么。巴克莱预计九月加息，十二月再加一次。你如何看待接下来的路径？

subtitles.en: So, we're still in the wait and see camp because I think that the first step to clearing the way for a rate hike in September is of course having someone like the chair come out and say we're very much actively considering it if the data point to that in that direction.
subtitles.zh: 我们仍持观望态度，因为九月加息的第一步是主席明确表示，如果数据指向加息，我们会积极考虑。

subtitles.en: So, the onus is really on that next set of inflation data. I think the labor market data probably still take a backseat to it, even if you get a strong job support next this coming Friday, I'm not so sure that that really changes the game or a week one. That doesn't necessarily change the game much. I think it's squarely rests on what CPI and PPI look like, and then ultimately how that maps over to PCE.
subtitles.zh: 因此，关键在于下一组通胀数据。劳动力数据可能退居其次，即使周五就业数据强劲，也不一定改变大局。重点在于CPI和PPI，以及它们如何映射到PCE。

subtitles.en: So, I do think that if it's firm or a little bit hot, that probably does give you a lock for September, but we have to wait and see what the rest of the FOMC says. So, it's still probably a little bit too early to assume that's going to be the case, but Worsh did mention that inflation is in his mind not going to come down just by itself back to target.
subtitles.zh: 如果数据稳健或略高，九月加息可能成定局，但还需等待FOMC其他成员的表态。现在假设还为时过早，但沃什提到，通胀不会自行回落到目标水平。
en_highlights: not going to come down just by itself

subtitles.en: So, at some point if you continue to see relatively sticky pressures, especially on the services side of the economy, which is where you're seeing a lot of stickiness and inflation, you're probably going to have to have the Fed respond to that sooner rather than later.
subtitles.zh: 如果服务领域持续出现通胀粘性压力，美联储可能不得不更早而非更晚做出回应。

clips.title: 加息预期升温：盈利却更强，工业板块能否继续领跑？
title_lines: 工业板块能否继续领跑？
title_highlights: 工业板块能否继续领跑？

subtitles.en: Yeah, that's a great question. I think, you know, we're pretty comfortable that, you know, we believed coming into the year. We were kind of done raising rates. I do think we've adjusted going into mid year, thinking that rates will increase. I think the equity markets have adjusted as well.
subtitles.zh: 好问题。年初我们认为加息已结束，但年中我们调整了预期，认为利率会上升。权益市场也已相应调整。

subtitles.en: But I would say they've adjusted because earnings growth has been incredibly strong. And obviously we're in one of the biggest innovation cycles we've ever been in. And I do think a lot of that continues. But rather than just focus on very narrow areas of the market like technology, we are much more focused on where AI could bring more efficiency and more, you know, more gains in the future.
subtitles.zh: 市场调整是因为盈利增长非常强劲，我们正处于最大的创新周期之一。我们认为这将继续。但我们更关注AI能带来效率提升和未来收益的领域，而非仅仅聚焦科技等狭窄板块。

subtitles.en: And I do think that there are industries that stand out to that. And the industrial has been a winner this year so far. We still really like that sector. I would just move down cap a little bit. There's a little bit more opportunity. I think multiples are better looking in the small and mid cap space for industrial. But I think they sit at a really interesting intersection, not only of the AI spend, but also of kind of the global re alignment of the supply chain.
subtitles.zh: 有些行业脱颖而出，工业板块今年表现领先，我们仍看好该板块。我们倾向于向中小盘倾斜，因为估值更具吸引力。工业板块处于AI支出和全球供应链重构的交汇点。

subtitles.en: I think that's one area of the market. We like a lot. There are others. Again, we've tended to shift a little bit more down cap. That's work for us. And again, it's a big world out there. And we do still think there's a lot of opportunity and emerging markets.
subtitles.zh: 这是我们非常看好的领域之一。我们倾向于向中小盘倾斜，这对我们有效。此外，全球市场广阔，我们仍认为新兴市场存在大量机遇。

clips.title: 剔除科技巨头：盈利依然惊人，医疗板块为何掉队？

subtitles.en: Well, even if you actually take out the big tech and the mega cap companies in earnings for second quarter earnings season, the numbers are still quite amazing. I mean, the breadth of gain so far, not just for the reporting the quarter, but for the year, the estimates for the year. That has really been, I think, a strong fundamental story for the market this year, at least in especially in the US, where, you know, breadth and revisions have been so strong across every sector.
subtitles.zh: 即使剔除大型科技和超大盘公司，第二季度盈利数据依然惊人。无论是本季度还是全年预期，盈利广度都非常强劲。这为今年市场提供了坚实的基本面支撑，尤其是在美国，各行业的盈利修正都非常强劲。

subtitles.en: Healthcare is really sort of that laggard still. But even with that, I mean, price has been pretty strong. It's been certainly, I think, a beneficiary to Anne's point about some of these areas that can really see a lot of efficiency gains. You're starting to see that trickle down a little bit. I think in terms of the broader profit backdrop and in the context of the market and performance, what's interesting is that if you go back in history, when you have earnings at this level in this zone, when they're, I mean, because we're approaching on a blended growth rate basis above 50% for just a second quarter, that tends to be consistent with weaker gains for the S&P 500.
subtitles.zh: 医疗保健仍是落后板块，但即便如此，价格表现也相当强劲。正如安妮提到的，一些领域能实现效率提升，这开始显现。有趣的是，从历史看，当盈利增速达到如此高水平，比如第二季度综合增速超过50%时，标普500的涨幅往往相对温和。

subtitles.en: It doesn't necessarily sound conventional, but when you think about a cycle getting a little bit longer, a little bit longer in the tooth, more mature, it does start to make a little bit more sense where you have more restrained gains, maybe more at the large cap level, maybe not as much at the small cap level. I think it's probably no surprise as to why the Russell 2000 has outperformed the S&P 500 over the past year. That has been a laggard in this bull market cycle. It's taken a lot more time to sort of get out of that sleepy phase. So that's why we would argue that this is still, you know, very much in keeping with what Anne said, still a relatively favorable backdrop for the broader market, not necessarily just that narrow group of mega caps.
subtitles.zh: 这听起来可能不太常规，但考虑到周期逐渐成熟，大盘涨幅受限，小盘股可能更有机会。罗素2000过去一年跑赢标普500并不意外，它在此前牛市中一直落后，现在才走出低迷。因此，我们认为整体市场环境依然有利，而不仅仅是少数超大盘股。
en_highlights: cycle getting a little bit longer

subtitles.en: I think it's interesting because we are at this unique time where we are seeing differentiation in financing. It is bringing more flexibility.
subtitles.zh: 有趣的是，我们正处于融资分化的独特时期，这带来了更多灵活性。

subtitles.en: I talked about earlier the corporate borrowing rate has kind of increased pretty, pretty steeply since the beginning of the year.

subtitles.en: Again, if you look at historic measures, it doesn't really stand out that much, but how quickly it's gone up does matter for companies.

subtitles.en: So I do think having availability of other types of financing can work. Now, you know, I'm a little hesitant to just to the thought that we don't know exactly when things really do slow down how all of the circular, circular financing will turn out.
subtitles.zh: 其他融资渠道可能有用，但我对循环融资在放缓时的表现有些保留。

subtitles.en: So I do have a little bit of reservation between what it looks like today and how helpful it can be for the economy today.
subtitles.zh: 我对当前状况及其对经济的帮助程度有所保留。

subtitles.en: But maybe the unknown unknowns that we will find out about later.
subtitles.zh: 但未来可能会有未知的风险。

subtitles.en: So I'm not an individual company analyst, but I think from a macro level, you do have to pay attention to the risks of some of the circular financing.

data_driven_lessons.source: KC桌面-视频号动态数据明细.csv, 114 rows, July 2026 local analysis
winning_patterns: 机构/人物权威 + 具体数字/资产 + 强问题，例如 高盛王逸：4-5万亿城市更新会拖住楼市吗
大机构/名人 + 被逼/陷阱/真相/转向 等张力词，例如 野村辜朝明：日本央行被逼到墙角
具体数据 + 政策动作疑问，例如 6月PMI释放积极信号，政府会加码吗
反常识判断 + 下一步条件，例如 低估值可能是价值陷阱，需等待政策转向消费
中国相关议题更容易获得点击，但表达要落在政策、需求、信心、估值、产业升级这些正向框架
外资或海外权威给出对中国更积极的判断时，反差本身就是主标题，不要埋在摘要里
让观众产生单一强反应：居然如此、终于有人说、他说的是真的吗、原来中国优势在这里
大实话角度来自表达者身份与观点反差；言行反差角度必须有公开动作或披露支撑
涉及中国比较优势时，优先把外国企业被迫调整、海外权威改口或中国优势被低估写成冲突
avoid_patterns: 过长的新闻句，尤其是 24 字以上还塞多个从句
只有 策略/机会/影响/前瞻/市场/风险 这类泛词，没有具体对象或张力
美国宏观泛标题如果没有美联储/鲍威尔等强锚点，点击明显弱
纯描述式标题，例如 某市场短期风险与长期催化剂，缺少问题和冲突
经济危机/金融危机/崩盘/崩溃 这类过硬负面财经词
把事实换成疑问号但没有反差，例如 回报路径在哪、未来如何、能否实现
陌生英文人名或机构全称占据第一行，却没有告诉观众这个人为什么值得听
把 Bloomberg LP 等来源或公司法律后缀误当成采访对象
没有公开证据却暗示嘉宾撒谎、操纵或言行不一
